name: ioctl_fat
synopsis: int ioctl(int fd, VFAT_IOCTL_READDIR_BOTH, struct __fat_dirent entry[2]);
int ioctl(int fd, VFAT_IOCTL_READDIR_SHORT, struct __fat_dirent entry[2]);
description: The ioctl system call manipulates metadata on FAT filesystems, such as file attributes, volume IDs, and directory entries, which are not accessible through standard system calls. It allows reading and writing of FAT-specific attributes and directory information using a file descriptor.

parameters.name: fd
parameters.description: File descriptor for a file, directory, or filesystem object

parameters.name: request
parameters.description: The ioctl command, such as FAT_IOCTL_GET_ATTRIBUTES or VFAT_IOCTL_READDIR_BOTH

parameters.name: arg
parameters.description: Pointer to argument data, which varies by request (e.g., uint32_t * for attributes, struct __fat_dirent for directory entries)

return_value.success: Returns 0 on success for most operations; for VFAT_IOCTL_READDIR_BOTH and VFAT_IOCTL_READDIR_SHORT, returns 1 if a new directory entry is read, or 0 if the end of the directory is reached
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: The file descriptor refers to a removed, but still open directory
The file descriptor does not refer to a directory
The file descriptor does not refer to an object in a FAT filesystem
